subject: runner on road
title: What If You Ran and Never Stopped?

scenes.text: What if you started running and never stopped? Your legs aren't the first thing to give out.
The most anyone has run in twenty-four hours is about one hundred ninety-nine miles, set in Italy in 2022.
In 2005, ultrarunner Dean Karnazes ran three hundred fifty miles in about eighty hours, with no sleep at all.
By then the brain is the problem. Karnazes hallucinated, and even fell asleep while running.
In one survey of over a thousand mountain ultra finishers, eight in ten reported sleep-loss symptoms.
Keep going for months, and you hit a hard ceiling: about two and a half times your resting energy, because your gut can't absorb more food.

description:
What if you ran and never stopped? The 24-hour record is 319.6 km (198.6 miles), set by Aleksandr Sorokin in 2022. In 2005, Dean Karnazes ran 350 miles in about 80 hours without sleep, hallucinating and even falling asleep while running.
In a 2024 survey of 1,154 mountain ultramarathon finishers, 80% reported sleep-deprivation symptoms. Over months, a 2019 Science Advances study found humans can't sustain more than about 2.5 times their resting metabolic rate, a limit tied to how much food the gut can absorb.
